400: Joyful Reunion by Fei Tian Ye Xiang (Seven Seas) is a sweeping historical danmei novel full of court intrigue and slow-building devotion. Duan Ling has spent his childhood neglected and mistreated by his late mother's family, until a stranger named Lang Junxia arrives claiming to have been sent by the father Duan Ling never knew. Taken to the capital of the Liao Empire, he is pulled into a world of political schemes. It's a rich pick for readers who love palace drama and loyal protectors.
401: Soara and the House of Monsters by Hidenori Yamaji (Seven Seas) is a gentle, inventive fantasy about building a new life. Soara, an orphan raised by knights to fight monsters, finds her sword skills unneeded once peace is declared. Instead she joins Krik, a dwarf who leads the Monster Architects, designing and building homes suited to all kinds of creatures. It's a cozy, creative read for fans of found family and fantasy worlds with clever practical details.
403: Stray Little Devil by Kotaro Mori (DrMaster) is a playful fantasy comedy with a magical-school feel. Schoolgirl Pam Akumachi casts a spell to summon a devil, and it works a little too well, pulling her into the Spirit World. Her only known way home is through Remy, who tells her she'll have to become a full-fledged devil by passing the devils' own school system. It's a cute, light read for fans of fish-out-of-water fantasy and spunky heroines.
404: Free Life Fantasy Online: Immortal Princess by Akisuzu Nenohi (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted VR-game fantasy comedy. Kotone gets a copy of the virtual reality game Free Life Fantasy Online from her younger sister and jumps in without knowing what she's doing. As a total novice, she accidentally builds a nearly impossible character and starts the game as a zombie. It's a fun, easygoing read for anyone who enjoys game-world adventures with an underdog twist.
405: From the Red Fog by Mosae Nohara (Yen Press) is a dark, atmospheric historical thriller set in Victorian London. Young Lewis grows up in the shadows of the city's back alleys, raised by a mother who hides a terrible secret, and he inherits an unsettling fascination with death. As he grows, his path winds through a London full of crime and danger. It's a gripping choice for readers who like gothic mysteries and morally complicated leads.
406: Missile Happy! by Miki Kiritani (Tokyopop) is a sweet, comedic shojo romance. Fifteen-year-old Mikako lives with her older sister Megumi, who is planning an arranged marriage to a man Mikako has never met. Determined to find out who he really is, Mikako moves into the same apartment building as him and slowly starts falling for him herself. It's a light, charming read for fans of awkward crushes and complicated family setups.
407: Momogumi Plus Senki by Eri Sakondo (Tokyopop) is a playful supernatural comedy that riffs on the folktale of Momotaro. Yuki, a trouble-magnet transfer student, learns that he's the reincarnation of the legendary Peach Boy. To break an ogres' curse before he turns eighteen, he has to hunt ogres hiding at his school, alongside three companions known as Dog, Monkey, and Pheasant. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy folklore twists, action, and goofy banter.
408: Tales of the Kingdom by Asumiko Nakamura (Yen Press) is an elegant, fable-like fantasy with a quiet emotional pull. When an assassination attempt on the young Dao fails because the king himself steps in, Dao is willing to accept any terms to stay alive, only to be surprised by the service he's asked to perform in the king's private chamber. Both men carry painful pasts and roles in the kingdom's future. It's a lovely choice for readers who appreciate striking art and slow, thoughtful storytelling.
409: Gangsta: Cursed. EP_Marco Adriano by Kohske (Viz Media) is a gritty action drama and prequel spin-off of Gangsta. It turns back the clock to the earlier life of Marco Adriano, one of the Twilights, the drug-enhanced fighters who are both feared and used by the world around them, digging into the violence and hard choices that shaped him. It's a strong pick for fans of the main series and anyone who likes dark, character-driven crime stories.
410: Generation Witch by Isaki Uta (Seven Seas) is a gentle slice-of-life fantasy set in a world much like our own. About one percent of people are witches, and while ordinary folks often envy them, magic can be more of a burden than a gift. The series follows teenage witches as they navigate school, friendships, and everyday life alongside spirits, spell circles, and broomsticks. It's a relaxed, thoughtful read for fans of quiet magic and coming-of-age stories.
411: Monthly in the Garden with My Landlord by Yodokawa (Yen Press) is a warm, low-key yuri slice of life. After a breakup, manga editor Suga Asako rents a detached house with a garden and a workroom, hoping for a fresh start. Then she discovers that her landlady lives in the attic, a detail the contract never quite made clear. It's a cozy, grown-up read for anyone who enjoys gentle romance between adults and the small rhythms of daily life.
412: Akihabara@Deep by Ira Ishida (Anime Works) is a quirky action story rooted in Tokyo's otaku culture. A group of misfits who met through an online advice site band together in Akihabara and launch a tiny tech startup called Akihabara@Deep. When they create a groundbreaking AI search engine, a powerful corporation decides it wants their work for itself. It's a fun, underdog-flavored read for anyone who enjoys geek culture, tech intrigue, and found-family teams.
413: Testarotho by Kei Sanbe (CMX) is a dark fantasy action series steeped in religious conflict. Garrincha is a feared inquisitor of Neo Arsen, working to bring heretics to the Arsenal faith alongside his loyal friend Leonedus, a nun named Capria, and their healer Socrates. Their mission grows personal when Sabati, an assassin who defected to the heretic sect Materia, comes after Leonedus, her childhood friend. It's a solid pick for fans of grim, sword-swinging fantasy with tangled loyalties.
414: Tetragrammaton Labyrinth by Ei Itou (Seven Seas) is a gothic action-horror series set in an alternate, industrial London around 1900. Scotland Yard won't touch extraordinary crimes, so that work falls to Meg Cross, a nun skilled in exorcism, and Angela, her eternally youthful partner. Together they hunt demons and bring demon summoners to justice. It's a stylish read for fans of Victorian occult adventures and supernatural detective stories.
415: Angel Cup by Jae-ho Youn and Dong-wook Kim (Tokyopop) is an energetic sports drama about girls' soccer in Korea. When So-jin Lee transfers to Han Shin High School and gets insulted by the boys' varsity team, she answers by forming a girls' soccer team of her own. The Han Shin High Blue Angels take on rival teams while juggling everyday school life. It's a spirited, upbeat read for fans of underdog teams and sports stories with plenty of attitude.
417: Animeta! by Yaso Hanamura (J-Novel Club) is a heartfelt workplace drama about the people who draw anime. Shin Mashiro has always loved drawing, and she takes a job at an animation studio as a brand-new in-between animator, where she quickly learns how demanding the work is, and how much skill and passion goes into every frame. It's a rewarding read for anime fans curious about the industry and anyone who enjoys stories about chasing a creative dream.
418: Apple Black by Odunze Oguguo (Saturday AM) is a bold, high-energy fantasy action series. Long ago, humans gained sorcery from "Black" fruits that fell from a tree in the sky, and that power is now passed down through bloodlines. Sano, raised in isolation and blessed with a mysterious arm, is said to be a destined figure whose power could save or doom the world, and after joining a sorcerers' guild he struggles to control it. It's a great pick for fans of classic shonen-style battles and big magic systems.
419: The Country Without Humans by Iwatobineko (Seven Seas) is a quietly moving sci-fi drama with a storybook feel. Shii is the only human left in a city run by machines. While fleeing a sinister figure called Triangle Head, she meets a gentle golem named Bulb, and the two have to survive long enough to become friends. It's a lovely choice for readers who enjoy post-apocalyptic settings with a soft heart and an unlikely bond at the center.
420: Nameless Asterism by Kina Kobayashi (Seven Seas) is a tender, tangled yuri romance with a light comedic touch. Tsukasa, Nadeshiko, and Mikage have been close friends since junior high, and Tsukasa has quietly had a crush on Nadeshiko for almost a year. She keeps it to herself to protect their friendship, until she learns that Nadeshiko has feelings for Mikage. It's a sweet, relatable read for anyone who enjoys complicated crushes and heartfelt school romance.
421: Necromance by Yuuki Doumoto (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure with a bittersweet romantic heart. After defeating the Demon King, the hero Shibuki is cursed with undeath and can no longer touch his beloved priestess, Safi. When he learns the Demon King actually survived, he gathers a new team of adventurers to finish the job and lift the curse. It's a fun pick for readers who like quest stories, quirky parties, and a love story with real obstacles.
422: Ninin ga Shinobuden by Ryoichi Koga (Infinity Studios) is a goofy, rapid-fire ninja comedy. Kaede is an ordinary high school girl whose life turns strange when Shinobu, a hopelessly clumsy ninja trainee, is sent to steal her underwear as part of a training mission. Instead of enemies, the two become friends, and Kaede gets pulled into the chaos of a very odd ninja school. It's a silly, absurd read for fans of gag manga and offbeat humor.
423: No Matter What You Say, Furi-san Is Scary! by Seiichi Kinoue (Seven Seas) is a sweet romantic comedy built on misunderstandings. Taira Namito gets nervous around his tough-looking classmate Furi Youko, convinced she's terrifying. In reality, Furi is gentle and has a crush on him, but he's far too intimidated to notice. It's a light, feel-good read for fans of shy romance and gentle school comedy.
424: Beauty and the Beast of Paradise Lost by Kaori Yuki (Kodansha) is a dark, lavish fairy-tale retelling. Belle's light purple hair marks her as an outsider, and after a mysterious beast in the forest takes her mother, her father locks her away for her own protection. Years later she escapes into the woods and meets the beast again, only to find there's more to him than the stories say. It's a perfect pick for fans of gothic romance and Kaori Yuki's ornate art.
425: Bird Kiss by Eun Ah Park (Tokyopop) is a bubbly romantic comedy manhwa with a fairy-tale opening. Miyoul, a middle schooler, is head over heels for a high schooler named Guelin and will go to great lengths to win his attention. Unfortunately for her plans, her devoted classmate Heerack, who has had a crush on her for ages, keeps getting in the way. It's a playful read for fans of love triangles and over-the-top school romance.
426: Blackguard by Ryo Hanada (Kodansha) is a dark post-apocalyptic action series from the creator of Devils' Line. Ape-like creatures that feed on humans roam the land, spreading a mysterious virus with their bites, while humanity survives in aerial cities defended by special units called Guards. Minami, a young Guard with a blank stare, fights so recklessly that people treat him as a messiah. It's a tense, moody read for fans of monster survival stories and grim sci-fi.
427: Blade of the Moon Princess by Tatsuya Endo (Viz Media) is a stylish sci-fi action adventure from the creator of Spy x Family. Princess Kaguya Takenouchi is heir to the moon's Silver Court, though not the heir her mother's retainers hoped for. When the empress falls ill amid a wave of terrorist attacks, Kaguya resolves to protect her people herself. It's a fast, fun read for anyone who enjoys sword fights, futuristic settings, and a determined heroine.
429: The Skull Man by Kazuhiko Shimamoto (Tokyopop) is a dark, pulpy action thriller reimagining Shotaro Ishinomori's 1970 classic. Tatsuo Kagura, taken in by a yakuza clan after his parents were murdered, sets out to find the shadowy power behind Japan's industry, finance, and politics. Meanwhile, a masked killer known as the Skull Man is carrying out a string of murders, and a detective agency is on the case. It's a strong pick for fans of retro tokusatsu heroes and gritty, mystery-driven action.
430: The Strange Adventure of a Broke Mercenary by Mine (Seven Seas) is a down-to-earth fantasy adventure. After the mercenaries who raised him fall in a brutal battle, Loren is left alone and turns to adventuring to make a living. His new start is rocky, and the only one who truly sees his worth is Lapis, a priest, so the two learn to rely on each other to survive. It's a solid pick for readers who like grounded swordsmen and slow-building partnerships.
432: Peigenz by Park Sung Woo (Infinity Studios) is an action-packed manhwa about mutants and the hunters who track them. In the early twenty-first century, a sudden rise in genetic mutations gives some people strange abilities, and society pushes them away, so the government secretly works with a team of mutant bounty hunters called the Peigenz. When high school student Jay Berell gets caught up in their fight with a serial killer, her own powers awaken. It's a fun read for fans of superpowered action.
433: Brain Powered by Yoshiyuki Tomino (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi mecha adventure from the creator of Mobile Suit Gundam. An ancient alien structure called the Orphan has been unearthed from the sea floor, bringing with it living, organic mecha and a threat to the whole planet. Young pilot Yuu Isami finds himself caught between the people trying to unlock the Orphan's power and those determined to stop it. It's a good pick for fans of classic giant-robot stories and the anime it accompanies.
434: Broken Angels by Setsuri Tsuzuki (Tokyopop) is a supernatural drama with an emotional, healing core. High schooler Sunao Fujiwara is often mistaken for a boy because of the way she dresses, and she can control water at will. She seems aloof, but she quietly serves as a counselor for people struggling with painful pasts, alongside the cross-dressing school nurse Shizuki and the affectionate Kureha. It's a thoughtful pick for readers who like gentle supernatural stories about helping others heal.
435: Phantom Dream by Natsuki Takaya (Tokyopop) is an early supernatural action series from the creator of Fruits Basket. Tamaki Ichinomiya is the heir to a line of exorcists who battle the dark spirits that feed on human despair and possess the vulnerable. Balancing that duty with an ordinary life and his bond with his close friend Hira is far from easy. It's a fine choice for Takaya fans and readers who enjoy emotional, character-focused supernatural battles.
436: The White Cat's Revenge as Plotted from the Dragon King's Lap by Kureha (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny isekai fantasy romance. Ruri has always lived in the shadow of her childhood friend Asahi, who charms everyone around her, and when the two are summoned to another world, it's Asahi everyone wants. Ruri slips away, and a magical bracelet turns her into a white cat who winds up on the lap of the Dragon King himself. It's a cozy read for fans of fluffy fantasy and slow-burn romance.
437: The World of Narue by Tomohiro Marukawa (CPM) is a lighthearted sci-fi romantic comedy. Middle schooler Kazuto Iizuka finds the courage to ask out his classmate Narue Nanase, only to discover that she's half alien and comes with some very unusual baggage. Their sweet, awkward relationship grows amid space visitors, giant robots, and everyday school life. It's a charming pick for readers who like gentle romance with a dash of science fiction.
438: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? Familia Chronicle Episode Freya by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure spin-off of the DanMachi series. Set long before Bell Cranell arrives in Orario, it follows Freya, the goddess of beauty, whose overprotective familia keeps her confined at home, so Freya slips away on her own to search for her Odr, her fated soulmate. It's a great pick for DanMachi fans curious about one of the series' most intriguing figures.
439: Cat Paradise by Yuji Iwahara (Yen Press) is a lively supernatural action series with a lot of feline charm. Yumi Hayakawa and her cat Kansuke enroll at Matabi Academy, a school where students can keep their cats in the dorms. They soon get swept into an ancient battle against Kaen, a long-sealed demon cat, alongside the student council that secretly defends the academy. It's a fun, fast read for cat lovers and fans of school-based supernatural adventures.
440: Jack the Ripper: Hell Blade by Je-Tae Yoo (Seven Seas) is a dark historical action manhwa with a supernatural edge. In 1888, the Ripper murders terrify London, and young detectives Roy and Harold are assigned to the case. They're joined by Ian, a Church of England representative who seems to know more about the killings than he lets on, while Roy's lover Susan faces troubles of her own. It's a gripping pick for fans of Victorian mysteries and gothic horror.
442: Juline by Narumi Kakinouchi (Chix Comix) is a playful martial arts action comedy from the creator of Vampire Princess Miyu. Juline is heir to the Kenga ninja clan, though she's far more interested in winning her handsome guardian's heart. When a mysterious new clan called the Black Pearl begins kidnapping members of the other clans, she has to team up with rivals to find out what's going on. It's a fun read for fans of classic kung fu heroines and lighthearted action.
444: Punch! by Rie Takada (Viz Media) is a bouncy shojo romantic comedy with a martial arts twist. Elle Nagahara comes from a family of martial arts champions, but she wants nothing to do with fighting. All she wants is a normal teenage life, until she crosses paths with a strange street fighter who turns everything upside down. It's a quick, fun read for fans of feisty heroines and energetic school romance.
445: Queens by Sung-Hyen Ha (Tokyopop) is a goofy, offbeat romantic comedy manhwa. Pil-Hyun Jung is a sweet, feminine-looking boy who loves making teddy bears, and he decides it's time to toughen up and become a "Real Man." After a chance run-in at a comic shop, he becomes the disciple of a manhwa artist who turns out to be a woman living with two attractive roommates. It's a silly, lighthearted read for fans of cross-cultural comedy and messy crushes.
447: Comic Party by Sekihiko Inui (Tokyopop) is a cheerful comedy about the world of fan-made comics. Art student Kazuki Sendo is dragged by his enthusiastic otaku friend Taishi to Comic Party, a huge doujinshi convention, and soon decides to try making his own comics. His new passion doesn't sit well with his childhood friend Mizuki, who isn't a fan of the otaku scene. It's a fun, affectionate read for anyone who loves conventions, fan culture, and creative underdogs.
448: Correspondence from the End of the Universe by Menota (Seven Seas) is a gentle, romantic sci-fi workplace drama. Marko, a young Russian university student, just wants to finish his studies and spend more time with his fiancee. Instead, he's abducted by aliens and handed a ten-year work assignment far from Earth, where he has to make the best of it and learn to work with his strange new colleagues while longing for home. It's a sweet, quirky read for fans of cozy space stories.
449: Crazy Love Story by Lee Vin (Tokyopop) is a moody, emotional romance manhwa. Jin Sung Moo works hard to keep his feelings hidden, while Shin Hae Jung lives life entirely on her own terms. When their paths collide, along with that of a stylish guy named Jimmy and his souped-up motorcycle, things get complicated fast. It's a good fit for readers who like intense, character-driven teen romance with a rebellious streak.
450: Croquis Pop by KwangHyun Seo and JinHo Ko (Yen Press) is a fun fantasy action manhwa about the power of storytelling. Da-Il lands a job with a famous comic creator despite having no artistic talent. Then he meets Mu-Huk, a ghost whose form depends on Da-Il's creativity, and learns he has the rare skills of a Croquer, someone who can enter the Dead Zone and reshape the stories of vengeful ghosts. It's a lively read for fans of supernatural battles with a creative twist.
451: Real/Fake Princess by Yi Huan (DrMaster) is a romantic historical fantasy set during China's Song dynasty. During a rebellion, an infant princess is entrusted to a commoner who escapes with her. Ten years later, the royal house searches for the missing girl, and advisor Wu Zhong Lu finds a peasant girl named Zhi Li who may be the princess, but she isn't eager to accept her new status, since it would separate her from Tan Hui, the boy she loves. It's a sweet pick for fans of palace romance.
452: Twinkle Stars by Natsuki Takaya (Yen Press) is a tender shojo romance from the creator of Fruits Basket. Sakuya Shiina, president of her high school's stargazing club, receives a pink dress on her eighteenth birthday from Chihiro, a mysterious boy who shows up at her party. When Chihiro enrolls at her school, an unusual bond begins to grow between them. It's a gentle, emotional read for Takaya fans and anyone who loves quiet, heartfelt romance.
453: Ultimate Venus by Takako Shigematsu (Go! Comi) is a breezy shojo romantic comedy with a rags-to-riches setup. After her mother dies, Yuzu Yamashita is left homeless with nowhere to turn, until she's whisked away to claim a family fortune she never knew existed, and starts a new life in a huge mansion full of handsome young men. It's a fun, frothy read for fans of Cinderella-style stories and lighthearted romance.
454: Kemono Friends a la Carte by Kemono Friends Project (Yen Press) is a cheerful comedy anthology set in the world of Kemono Friends. The stories follow Kyururu and Serval as they meet and play with all kinds of lively animal-girl Friends. Some chapters are chaotic little adventures, while others are lazy, relaxing days in the park. It's a sweet, easygoing read for fans of the anime and anyone who enjoys short, cute slice-of-life stories.
455: Utopia's Avenger by Oh Se Kwon (Tokyopop) is a rollicking action manhwa that mixes feudal fantasy with sci-fi gadgets. Bounty hunter Hong Gil-Dong and his young acolyte Danu rescue Ju Sanghui, a merchant's abducted daughter, and set out to escort her home past bandits, assassins, and monsters. Along the way, Gil-Dong claims to be the legendary founder of the lost kingdom of Yuldo, and he seems to be growing younger every day. It's a fun pick for fans of swashbuckling adventure with a folklore twist.
456: KimiKiss: Various Heroines by Taro Shinonome (Tokyopop) is a sweet seinen romance based on the dating-sim game. High schooler Kouichi Aihara has never been kissed, and the series explores how things might unfold with each of the girls in his life. Each volume focuses on a different heroine's story, from childhood friends to new classmates. It's a light, easygoing read for fans of the game or anime and anyone who enjoys episodic school romance.
457: Kiruru Kill Me by Yasuhiro Kano (Seven Seas) is a quirky romantic comedy with an action-packed twist. Aoi Nemo is a celebrated medical prodigy who is charming in public but can't talk openly with women, especially Kiruru Akaumi, the girl he's fallen for. When he learns she's an assassin, he comes up with a wild plan: hire her to kill him, so they can finally spend time together, trusting his medical genius to keep him alive. It's a goofy, fast-paced read for fans of offbeat love stories.
458: Culdcept by Shinya Kaneko (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure based on the card-battle video game. Najaran is an apprentice Cepter, someone who can summon creatures and spells from magical cards, and she travels with Goligan, her worrywart talking staff. Together they set out to save the Culdcept, the legendary book in which the goddess Culdra once kept all the cards. It's a fun read for fans of card-battle stories and lighthearted quest fantasy.
459: Reborn as a Polar Bear: The Legend of How I Became a Forest Guardian by Houki Kusano (Yen Press) is a cozy, funny isekai fantasy. After a climber falls off a mountain, he wakes up in another world in the body of a polar bear. He soon finds himself protecting two young werewolf sisters while figuring out how to survive the dangers of the forest. It's a charming pick for readers who enjoy fluffy found-family stories and lighthearted reincarnation adventures.
460: Days on Fes by Kanato Oka (Yen Press) is an upbeat slice-of-life story about the joy of live music. Kanade Sora has never been to a music festival, but her friend Otoha talks her into going with the promise that Kanade's favorite band will be playing. She ends up having far more fun than she expected and starts thinking about bigger, overnight festivals. It's a feel-good read for music lovers and anyone who enjoys stories about friends discovering a new passion together.
461: Kurogane by Kei Toume (Del Rey) is a moody samurai action series with a steampunk edge. Jintetsu, a teenage assassin, is killed by wild dogs and brought back to life as a partly mechanical cyborg by a former samurai turned inventor. Now he wanders as a hired sword with Haganemaru, his talking blade, trying to escape his past while protecting those who need it. It's a strong pick for fans of wandering swordsman tales and atmospheric, character-driven action.
462: Romance Papa by Youngran Lee (Net Comics) is a funny, heartfelt family drama and romance manhwa. Sangbum is a germophobic plastic surgeon with no interest in women, until he learns that sperm he donated in medical school resulted in a thirteen-year-old daughter, Myunghae. When her foster parents die, she moves in with him, and he is completely unprepared for fatherhood, while Myunghae has school romance troubles of her own. It's a warm read for fans of unlikely-family comedies.
463: Rose Hip Rose by Tohru Fujisawa (Tokyopop) is a high-octane action thriller from the creator of GTO. Kasumi Asakura seems like an ordinary high school girl, but she's secretly Rose Hip, an amnesiac anti-terrorist specialist who takes on criminals with martial arts and firearms. When classmate Shouhei Aiba stumbles onto her secret, the two get caught up in a plot by an extremist group to seize hostages and destroy a government building. It's a fast, explosive read for action movie fans.
464: Defeating the Demon Lord's a Cinch (If You've Got a Ringer) by Tsukikage (Yen Press) is a clever fantasy light novel with a behind-the-scenes hero. Ten years into a war against the Demon Lord Kranos, the Kingdom of Ruxe summons a Holy Warrior from another world. The Church assigns Ares Crown, a jaded and very high-level priest, to join the hero's inexperienced party and secretly keep them alive from the shadows. It's a fun read for fans of competent, world-weary leads and party-adventure fantasy.
465: Run on Your New Legs by Wataru Midori (Yen Press) is an inspiring sports drama about starting over. Shouta Kikuzato lost most of his leg in an accident just as he and his friend had gotten into their dream soccer school, ending his playing career. After a moment of running to save a child, a prosthetist offers him a running blade, and a whole new possibility opens up. It's a moving, energetic read for sports fans and anyone who loves stories about resilience and rediscovering joy.
466: Demonizer Zilch by Milan Matra (Yen Press) is a dark supernatural action series. Sixteen-year-old Haruomi Io keeps dreaming about the childhood accident that took his mother, sister, and childhood friend. When he's attacked by a mysterious girl and rescued by a demon named Zilch, who grants him strange powers, he's pulled into a war between demons and a secretive religious organization. It's a gripping pick for fans of demon-contract stories with plenty of mystery and intense battles.
467: Desert Coral by Wataru Murayama (ADV) is a portal fantasy adventure with a dreamy premise. High school student Naoto Saki has long dreamed of a fantasy world called Orgos. When the sorceress Lusia summons him there in the middle of a battle with her rival Camu, Naoto suddenly finds himself with a real body in that world, swept up in its conflicts. It's a fun read for fans of classic other-world adventures with magic, rivalries, and a touch of mystery.
468: Saint? No! I'm Just a Passing Beast Tamer! by Inumajin and iidatoy (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny isekai fantasy. Kanata Aldezia is a gifted prodigy everyone expects to become a Saint, the rarest and most honored calling. But Kanata has other plans: in her previous life, illness kept her bedridden, so now that she's healthy, she's determined to become a Beast Tamer and pet every fluffy creature she can find. It's a cozy pick for animal lovers and fans of lighthearted reincarnation stories.
470: Witch Life in a Micro Room by Akitaka (Yen Press) is a cozy, funny slice-of-life fantasy. Madge and Lilika are beginner witches sharing a tiny 99-square-foot apartment in the big city. They take low-paying jobs and live mostly on cabbage, scrimping and saving in hopes of affording a pet, more grimoires, and maybe some meat. It's a charming, relatable read for anyone who's ever stretched a budget, and for fans of gentle magic and close friendships.
471: Legend by SooJung Woo (Yen Press) is a time-slip fantasy action manhwa rooted in Korean legend. Long ago, a selfish king summoned the monstrous Bulkirin into the world, until a hero defeated it with a legendary sword. In the present day, eighth grader Eun-Gyo Sung, suspended for fighting, runs away from home and is abruptly kidnapped into the past by a mysterious stranger named No-Ah. It's an adventurous read for fans of tough heroines, sword fights, and fantasy steeped in history.
472: Legendz by Rin Hirai (Viz Media) is a kid-friendly fantasy action series tied to the monster-battling franchise. Young Shu Kaname gets his hands on a Talispod, a device that can revive legendary creatures, and ends up awakening Shiron, the mighty Windragon. The two become partners and find themselves facing rival battlers and plenty of trouble. It's a fun, fast read for younger fans of monster-partner adventures in the style of Pokemon and Digimon.
473: Les Bijoux by Jo Eun-Ha (Tokyopop) is a dark, dramatic fantasy manhwa about rebellion against cruel rulers. In a world where the ruling Habits brutally oppress the commoners known as Spars, a strange child is born to a dwarf and a hunchback, one who can shift between male and female forms as Lapis and Lazuli. When the cruel Habit lord Diamond destroys their family, Lapis vows revenge and sets out to overthrow the tyrants. It's a gripping pick for fans of revenge stories and offbeat fantasy.
475: Sarai by Masahiro Shibata (Comics One) is a gritty post-apocalyptic action adventure. In a bleak future ravaged by genetic disorders, most creatures are deformed and people rarely live past seventeen. Sarai is a teenage "battle-maid" who takes on any job that comes her way, from housecleaning to fighting off invaders. It's a strong pick for readers who like tough heroines, harsh survival settings, and plenty of fast, kinetic action.
476: Sarasah by Ryu Ryang (Yen Press) is a romantic fantasy manhwa with a time-slip twist. High schooler Ji-Hae has had a crush on Seung-Hyu for years, but things go terribly wrong when a fall down a flight of stairs ends her life. Sympathetic gods send her back centuries into the body of her past self, where she disguises herself as a boy to join the Hwa Rang warriors, partly to get close to Seung-Hyu's past self. It's a fun pick for fans of historical romance and cross-dressing heroines.
478: Dokebi Bride by Marley (Net Comics) is a haunting, atmospheric fantasy drama steeped in Korean folklore. After the death of her grandmother, a shaman, young Sunbi is left with a difficult inheritance: the ability to see spirits and the dokebi, the mischievous goblins of Korean legend. As she struggles with grief, she has to come to terms with a gift that keeps pulling her toward the spirit world. It's a striking read for fans of folklore-rich fantasy and quiet, emotional storytelling.
479: Scarlet Soul by Kira Yukishiro (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure about exorcists guarding the line between worlds. In the kingdom of Nohmur, exorcists long ago drove back the demons and sealed the way to the underworld of Ruhmon. Sisters Lys and Rin, heirs of the powerful Shirano family, protect that barrier with Hikaten, the Sword of a Hundred Souls, but when nearby villages come under violent attack, the sacred sword begins reacting to something unknown. It's a lovely pick for fans of sisterly bonds and demon-fighting fantasy.
480: School Zone Girls by Ningiyau (Seven Seas) is a goofy, offbeat yuri comedy. Rei Yokoe and Kei Sugiura have been best friends since middle school, and they fight off boredom by getting into all kinds of strange mischief around their school. Underneath all the silliness, the two are also in love with each other. It's a fun, quick read for fans of oddball humor, school antics, and sweet girls' love.
481: Louie the Rune Soldier by Ryo Mizuno (ADV) is a rowdy fantasy comedy set in a classic sword-and-sorcery world. Louie is a brawny, hot-headed young man who would much rather punch his way through problems, yet he's training as a sorcerer. When he joins a party of three capable young women, he becomes their unlikely spellcaster, and chaos follows wherever they go. It's a silly, adventurous read for fans of tabletop-style fantasy and ensemble comedy.
483: Yokai Rental Shop by Shin Mashiba (Seven Seas) is an eerie supernatural mystery with a streak of humor, from the creator of Nightmare Inspector. Hiiragi learns he has a half-brother he's never met, and when he tracks him down, he finds a young man wrapped head to toe in bandages who runs a very unusual store. Its hidden side lets customers in the know hire yokai spirits for supernatural tasks, but only after signing a bloody pact. It's a great pick for fans of spooky, episodic folklore stories.
484: Mad Love Chase by Kazusa Takashima (Tokyopop) is a madcap supernatural comedy. Kaito, the Prince of Hell, runs away to the human world to escape an arranged marriage, taking his cat Levun along; he disguises himself as a skinny teenager, while Levun becomes a curvy school nurse. Unfortunately for Kaito, the King of Hell sends three lackeys to drag him home, and his fiancee comes looking for him too. It's a silly, chaotic read for fans of over-the-top comedy and demon-world shenanigans.
485: Dream Saga by Megumi Tachikawa (Tokyopop) is a whimsical shojo fantasy adventure inspired by Japanese mythology. Young Yuuki Wakasa receives a magical red stone that lets her enter the dream world of Takamagahara while she sleeps and return when she wakes. There she learns that the sun goddess Amaterasu is trapped, and unless she's rescued, light will vanish from both worlds. It's a charming pick for readers who enjoy magical quests, mythological settings, and classic shojo adventure.
486: Eternity by Park Jin-Ryong (Tokyopop) is an action-comedy manhwa inspired by the legends of ancient China's Three Kingdoms era. In the year 184, three leaders who rose up against an oppressive government were all killed. Centuries later, seventeen-year-old shaman Aram Ko is searching for their reincarnations, bound by an old promise that ties the women of her family to one of those heroes. It's a fun pick for readers who like reincarnation stories, history-inspired fantasy, and lively banter.
487: Evil's Return by Hwan Shin (Tokyopop) is a supernatural action manhwa with a romantic thread. Yumi is a Pure Blood, a young woman who can take on the pain of others, and because the fate of the world depends on whose children she bears, both Heaven and Hell want her. Two people step up to protect her: a mystical warrior named Hyun and a school freshman who has just fallen for her. It's a dramatic read for fans of good-versus-evil battles and protective heroes.
489: Fairy Tale Battle Royale by Soraho Ina (Seven Seas) is a dark, twisted fantasy action series. Aoba Kunihara is a bullied loner who escapes into Alice in Wonderland, and after her cherished work is destroyed, she finds a mysterious contract and wishes to be friends with her whole class. The next day her classmates eagerly seek her out, but she's pulled into a decaying Wonderland, dressed as Alice and surrounded by zombified soldiers. It's a gripping read for fans of death-game stories and fairy tales gone wrong.
490: Seraphic Feather by Hiroyuki Utatane and Yo Morimoto (Dark Horse) is a hard-edged sci-fi action series. An intact alien starship lies buried beneath the surface of the Moon, its technology tied to three powerful Emblem Seeds found on Earth. Sunao Oumi, stranded on the Moon and saving up to get home, agrees to escort two U.N. investigators, and quickly finds himself caught in violence as covert operatives try to seize the Seeds. It's a strong pick for fans of gritty space thrillers and classic nineties manga.
491: Shaolin Sisters by Narumi Kakinouchi (Tokyopop) is a kung fu action fantasy. Julin Kenga has always believed she was an orphan and an only child, until her fifteenth birthday, when the White Queen Bai Wang attacks her dojo, and her master, Yoh, reveals that Julin's father is alive and that she has two older sisters. With Bai Wang hunting her, Julin sets out to find her sisters and uncover the mystery of their father. It's a fun pick for fans of martial arts heroines and family quests.
493: ShutterBox by Tavisha Wolfgarth-Simons (Tokyopop) is a dreamy original English-language fantasy romance. Megan Amano, a college student in Santa Monica, dreams of Merridiah University, an afterlife school where spirits train to become muses for the living. Since Megan is still alive, she attends as an exchange student, but when she finds mysterious photos of the dream world on her digital camera, she starts questioning her own existence. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy surreal settings and gentle, artsy romance.
494: Sister and Giant: A Young Lady Is Reborn in Another World by Be-con (Yen Press) is an action-packed isekai fantasy with a yuri streak. After being reborn in a new world, Hinako turns down the overpowered abilities a goddess offers her. Instead, she becomes sworn sisters with a giant named Ellis, earning the nickname "Smallest Giant." The two are each searching for people who mattered deeply to them, and their strength brings both fame and trouble. It's a fun pick for fans of unusual partnerships and fantasy adventure.
495: Eclair by various authors (Yen Press) is a heartfelt yuri anthology full of short, sweet love stories between girls. Each chapter comes from a different creator, so the collection mixes school crushes, adult relationships, first confessions, and quiet everyday moments, all with a range of art styles. It's an easy series to dip into a story at a time. It's a lovely pick for longtime yuri fans and for newcomers looking to sample many different creators in one place.
496: I'm the Catlords' Manservant by Rat Kitaguni (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny comedy for cat lovers. High schooler Izumi Yukihara loses his parents and is left with their enormous debt. When he moves into a new home, its owners offer him an unusual way to pay it off: by serving their cats. It's a cozy, lighthearted read about pampered felines and their devoted human, perfect for anyone who has ever felt like their pet was really in charge.
497: My [Repair] Skill Became a Versatile Cheat, So I Think I'll Open a Weapon Shop by Ginga Hoshikawa (Seven Seas) is an easygoing fantasy adventure. Luke is a low-ranked adventurer whose only skill is Repair, and when his party abandons him in a dungeon, he has to use it to escape. Along the way the skill grows far stronger than anyone expected, and Luke starts dreaming of a quieter life running a weapon shop. It's a relaxed read for fans of underdog heroes and slow-life fantasy.
498: The Mimosa Confessions by Mei Hachimoku (Seven Seas) is a tender, thoughtful coming-of-age light novel from the author of The Tunnel to Summer, the Exit of Goodbyes. Sakuma lives in a dull suburb, and the brightest thing in his life is his talented, athletic best friend Ushio. Then Ushio shows up at school ready to live openly as a girl, and their friendship and Sakuma's own feelings are thrown into new territory. It's a moving read for fans of honest, emotional school stories about love and identity.
499: I Swear I Won't Bother You Again! by Reina Soratani (Seven Seas) is an emotional fantasy romance about second chances. Consumed by jealousy, the noble daughter Violette lashes out at her younger stepsister Maryjune and ends up imprisoned. Full of regret, she wishes she could go back to the day they first met and promise never to bother Maryjune again. Then she suddenly finds herself back in time, facing the same difficult family with a chance to choose differently. It's a heartfelt pick for fans of villainess redemption stories.
500: I Swear I Won't Bother You Again! by Reina Soratani (Seven Seas) is a gentle romantic fantasy about a villainess getting a second chance. Violette sits in a prison cell after lashing out at Maryjune, the half-sister her neglectful father brought home along with his mistress. When she finds herself back in the past, she resolves to step aside and stay out of everyone's way for good. It's a quiet, emotional read for fans of redemption stories and slow-building romance.
503: Am I Actually the Strongest? by Sai Sumimori (Kodansha) is a lighthearted isekai comedy about an overpowered hero who just wants some peace and quiet. A former shut-in is reborn as a prince in a world of magic, but a botched mana reading at birth labels him powerless, and his royal parents abandon him in a forest. He survives easily with barrier magic, gains a loyal Fenrir companion, and keeps trying to stay out of trouble. It's breezy fun for fans of easygoing, overpowered-protagonist fantasy.
504: Pick of the Litter by Yuriko Suda (Tokyopop) is a playful supernatural comedy with a big, odd family at its center. Riku arrived in Tokyo at age ten remembering nothing but his name, and five years later some strangely dressed visitors claim he's their long-lost brother and whisk him away to another world. There he finds a family with animal ears and tails who run a shop selling magical oddities. It's a cute, silly read for fans of found-family stories and kemonomimi charm.
505: Bride of the Barrier Master by Kureha (Yen Press) is a tender fantasy romance with a Cinderella heart. Hana has always lived in the shadow of her twin sister, whose spiritual gifts make her the pride of the family, while Hana is overlooked and treated as a burden. Everything changes when Saku Ichinomiya, the powerful head of the barrier masters, chooses Hana as his bride. It's a comforting read for fans of My Happy Marriage and slow, sweet romance.
506: The Haunted Bookstore by Shinobumaru (Seven Seas) is a warm, gently magical fantasy about books and the spirits who love them. Kaori is a human girl raised in the spirit world by Shinonome, a grumpy but caring spirit who runs a bookstore that lends stories to its supernatural customers. Each visitor arrives with a worry or a wish, and the right book often helps. It's a cozy, heartfelt read for book lovers and fans of Japanese folklore.
507: Seraph of the End by Takaya Kagami (Kodansha) is a dark supernatural prequel told in light novel form by the series' original creator. Set before the world falls, it follows sixteen-year-old Guren Ichinose as he enrolls at an elite school for magic users run by the powerful Hiragi family, where his own lesser clan is looked down on. Rivalries, secrets, and forbidden research simmer beneath the surface. It's a great pick for fans of the manga and anime who want Guren's backstory.
508: I Was Reincarnated as the Villainess in an Otome Game But the Boys Love Me Anyway! by Ataka (Tokyopop) is a sweet, funny villainess fantasy. On her tenth birthday, Mystia Aren remembers her past life and realizes she has been reborn as the villainess of a romance game she once played. Determined to avoid her doomed ending, she plans to break off her engagement, but her kindness keeps winning over the very boys she's trying to avoid. It's a light, charming read for fans of otome isekai.
509: Soul to Seoul by Jea Eun Kim (Tokyopop) is a shojo drama about friendship, identity, and first love. Kai and Spike are half-Korean best friends who feel out of place both at home and out in the world, and they lean on each other to get by. When they meet Sunil, a Korean exchange student, both boys find themselves drawn to her. It's an earnest, emotional manhwa for readers who like love triangles and stories about belonging.
511: Strawberry Marshmallow by Barasui (Seven Seas) is a laid-back slice-of-life comedy. Twenty-year-old Nobue spends her days lounging around, smoking, and hanging out with her little sister Chika and Chika's elementary school friends, including the endlessly mischievous Miu. Not much happens, and that's the point: the humor comes from small, silly everyday moments and the girls' sharp comic timing. It's a cozy, easygoing read for fans of Azumanga Daioh and Yotsuba&!
513: Kamiyadori by Kei Sanbe (Tokyopop) is a dark sci-fi action series set in a grim future. A biological plague is turning people into monsters called Kamiyadori, and a special unit known as the Right Arms, whose agents carry a strain of the virus that makes them superhumanly strong, is tasked with killing the infected before it spreads. Agents Jil and Vivi are good at the job, until they can't bring themselves to kill a young boy and his sister. It's gritty, fast-moving action from the creator of Erased.
515: Mujina Into the Deep by Inio Asano (Viz Media) is a sharp, offbeat seinen action series with a satirical streak. In the near future, human rights are no longer guaranteed but sold, and anyone who can't afford them becomes a mujina, a person no law protects. Some of the rightless turn that freedom into a career as elite assassins. It's stylish, darkly funny, and occasionally violent, a fresh turn for fans of Goodnight Punpun and Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction.
516: Hi, I'm a Witch, and My Crush Wants Me to Make a Love Potion by Eiko Mutsuhana (Yen Press) is a sweet, bittersweet fantasy romance. Rose, the Witch of the Lake, has quietly loved the knight Harij for years, so it stings when he shows up asking her to brew him a love potion. Rather than hand one over, she sends him off to gather ingredients, buying herself more time with him. It's a gentle, funny slow burn for readers who enjoy pining heroines and soft-hearted fantasy.
517: Daily Report About My Witch Senpai by Maka Mochida (Seven Seas) is a sweet, low-key magical romantic comedy. Misono has his share of everyday struggles, and his senpai Shizuka, a kind and easily flustered witch, is always ready to lend a hand. As he watches her zip around on her broom helping everyone else, he starts to worry she's wearing herself out, and wonders whether his protectiveness is simple respect or something more. It's a gentle, cozy read for fans of soft, slow-burn romance.
518: Spell of Desire by Tomu Ohmi (Viz Media) is a sultry paranormal romance for older readers. Kaoruko runs a quiet herb shop in a small seaside town, until a mysterious man in black named Kaname walks in and tells her she's a witch. Her powers are waking up, he says, and she'll need his help, and his protection, to control them. It's a moody, grown-up shojo romance from the creator of Midnight Secretary, best for readers who like their magic with plenty of heat.
520: April Showers Bring May Flowers by Roku Sakura (Yen Press) is a gentle, heartwarming high school romantic comedy. Hana Tabata is a shy first-year who is convinced she's plain, and she quietly arranges the classroom flowers every morning before anyone else arrives. One day Yosuke Ueno, the most popular boy in class, catches her at it and starts talking to her. It's a sweet, slow-blooming story for readers who love kind characters and the nervous joy of a first crush.
522: Just Like Mona Lisa by Tsumuji Yoshimura (Square Enix) is a thoughtful coming-of-age drama with a fantasy twist. In this world, people are born without a gender, and their bodies shift toward the one they want around age twelve. Hinase reached eighteen still content without one, until bubbly Ritsu and gentle Shiori both confess on the same day. It's a tender, quietly moving story about love and identity for readers who like character-driven romance.
523: The Savior's Book Café Story in Another World by Kyouka Izumi (Seven Seas) is a relaxed, cozy isekai about choosing a quieter life. Thirty-three-year-old Tsukina is whisked to a fantasy world to serve as its savior, but she turns the job down and negotiates for what she really wants: a cottage at the forest's edge and a book café of her own. Soon the captain of the royal knights becomes her first regular. It's a soothing, bookish read for fans of slow-life fantasy with a touch of romance.
526: Hell Is Dark with No Flowers by Yoru Michio and Ruka Todo (Yen Press) is an eerie supernatural mystery adapted from an award-winning novel. Seiji is a homeless college dropout cursed to sometimes see people as monsters, the visible shape of their sins. Then he meets Shiroshi, a striking young man in a kimono who offers him room and board in exchange for his help with a very unusual line of work. It's moody, atmospheric horror for readers who like yokai stories with a moral edge.
529: A Kingdom of Quartz by Bomhat (Kodansha) is a sweeping dark fantasy with gorgeous, painterly art. The Kingdom of Quartz is defended from demons by Angels, powerful winged warriors who serve the Goddess. Blue, an orphan girl born with strange black wings, dreams of joining them, and a chance meeting with a prince pulls her into court politics, danger, and adventure. It's a moody, beautifully drawn epic for readers who like angels-and-demons fantasy and a heroine who doesn't fit in.
530: Semantic Error by Jeosuri and Angy (Ize Press) is a sharp, funny campus romance. Sangwoo, a rule-bound computer science student, quietly drops a design major named Jaeyoung from a group project's credits for not contributing. Jaeyoung does not take it well, and the two keep colliding until their rivalry starts turning into something else. It's a lively enemies-to-lovers story for readers who enjoy prickly leads and plenty of banter.
531: The Skull Dragon's Precious Daughter by Ichi Yukishiro (Seven Seas) is a tender, bittersweet fantasy about an unlikely family. Little Eve is abandoned in a forest where creatures of every kind dump their trash, and there an aging dragon finds her and decides to raise her as his own. Eve grows up happy in his care, but their time together may not last as long as she hopes. It's a gentle, heart-tugging read for fans of Frieren and found-family stories.
532: Dead Rock by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a high-energy fantasy action series from the creator of Fairy Tail. In the demon world, an academy trains young demons to one day rule over humanity, and its principal is a being so powerful he calls himself God. Yakuto, a young demon descended from a black dragon, enrolls with one goal in mind: taking that principal down. It's loud, fast, and full of flashy battles, a great pick for fans of Mashima's big, bold shonen style.
534: Lullaby of the Dawn by Ichika Yuno (Tokyopop) is a lush, melancholy fantasy BL. On an island guarded by the kannagi, priests chosen by the gods to fight the monsters that rise from the black sea, the role is sacred but feared, because a kannagi's body is slowly worn away by the duty. When Alto and Elva are bound together by that calling, a deep and complicated bond begins to grow. It's a beautifully drawn, emotional slow burn for readers who love tragic fantasy romance.
535: The Fed-Up Office Lady Wants to Serve the Villainess by Nekotarou (Seven Seas) is a funny, warmhearted yuri-tinged isekai. Twenty-five-year-old Midori is burned out on office life when she's suddenly summoned into her favorite mobile game, not as the heroine but as the familiar of Lapis, its haughty, commoner-hating villainess. Knowing Lapis is fated for a grim end, Midori sets out to protect her and maybe soften her views along the way. It's a lively, sweet read for fans of devoted-servant villainess stories.
536: Akira Failing in Love by Shinta Harekawa (Viz Media) is a sweet, goofy countryside romantic comedy. Akira moves back to her old rural hometown for high school with a foolproof plan to win over Hajime, the childhood friend she's had a crush on for years. The trouble is that both of them are hopelessly clumsy when it comes to love. It's a warm, laugh-out-loud read for fans of awkward first romances and small-town charm.
538: Kusunoki's Garden of Gods by Enju (Yen Press) is a cozy, low-stakes supernatural slice of life. Minato Kusunoki is put in charge of a remote country house overflowing with evil spirits, but his unusual knack for purifying things clears them out. The newly cleansed home soon draws a parade of quirky local gods, and Minato settles into peaceful days spent with his divine new neighbors. It's a gentle, relaxing read for fans of Japanese folklore and slow-life stories.
539: I Want to Escape from Princess Lessons by Izumi Sawano, Uri Sugata, and Miru Yumesaki (Seven Seas) is a funny fantasy romance. Lettie has been engaged to Crown Prince Clarke since she was seven and has spent years stuck in princess lessons. When Clarke shows up at a royal ball with another woman, she assumes she's finally free and runs off to the countryside for a simple life, only for him to follow and insist the engagement is still on. It's a playful tug-of-war romance for fans of stubborn heroines.
540: Confessions of a Shy Baker by Masaomi Itou (Tokyopop) is a warm, grown-up slice-of-life BL. Toshimitsu runs a real estate business and bakes to unwind, and his longtime partner Gonta, a caregiver, is always happy to share the results. But Gonta is open about who he is, while Toshimitsu still keeps their relationship quiet, and that gap causes real friction. It's a tender, down-to-earth story about an established couple, with plenty of sweet treats along the way.
541: My Girlfriend is 8 Meters Tall by Wataru Mitogawa (Seven Seas) is a sweet, offbeat high school romantic comedy. Yumeji is surprised when his childhood friend Chieri transfers into his class, mostly because she now stands eight meters tall. Assigned as her helper, he guides her through a school that was never built for someone her size, from giant-sized mishaps to quietly tender moments. It's a goofy, good-natured read for fans of unusual romcoms with a big heart.
544: Chainsmoker Cat by Nyan Nyan Factory (Seven Seas) is a scruffy, deadpan slice-of-life comedy for grown-ups. Yani is a cat girl with a serious smoking habit, living in an apartment buried in ash, cigarette butts, and old takeout. She keeps swearing she'll quit, and she keeps caving almost immediately. It's a short-chapter, low-key gag manga with a soft spot for messy adult life, perfect for readers who like their cats grumpy and their humor dry.
545: Redmoon by Hwang Mi-Na (Comics One) is a sweeping sci-fi fantasy manhwa about love and war between humans and aliens. Taeyoung is an ordinary high school student until mysterious enemies attack him and equally mysterious allies come to his rescue. As another self begins to awaken inside him, he has to decide whether to accept the destiny everyone seems to expect of him. It's a dramatic, romantic classic of Korean shojo comics for fans of epic, old-school space fantasy.
546: The Devil Princess by Harunohi Biyori (Seven Seas) is a darkly funny fantasy about a very unholy saint. A demon who has always longed for the human world gets her wish when she's reborn as a baby girl into the royal family of a holy kingdom. Her loving family thinks she's a blessing, and soon everyone hails her as the prophesied Saint, while she quietly hides her demonic appetites behind an innocent smile. It's a mischievous, offbeat read for fans of villain-protagonist isekai.
547: Super Ball Girls by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Akira Hiramoto (Yen Press) is a weird, darkly comic sci-fi horror harem from the writer of Blue Lock and the artist of Prison School. Eita is stuck in a low-paying chocolate factory job when he finds a strange super ball on his walk home. He gives it a toss, a gorgeous woman appears, and soon he's caretaker to a whole group of beautiful but genuinely unsettling creature-girls. It's bizarre, unpredictable fun for readers who like their comedy with a creepy edge.
548: Touge Oni: Primal Gods in Ancient Times by Kenji Tsurubuchi (Yen Press) is a striking, hard-edged historical fantasy. In ancient Yamato, gods and humans still share the land, and powerful kami rule it, each with its own temper and sacred treasure. The priest En the Layman travels from shrine to shrine with his two young assistants, braving rough country, fearsome creatures, and the wrath of the gods themselves. It's a beautifully drawn, mythic adventure for older readers who enjoy Japanese folklore and intense action.
549: That's Not Love by Peko Watanabe (Kodansha) is a thoughtful, emotionally honest drama for adult readers from the creator of 1122: For a Happy Marriage. Two women who were friends in middle school reconnect as adults, and what starts as easy reminiscing begins to surface old, painful memories they never fully understood. Together they work through what happened and what it meant. Drawing on real events and Japan's #MeToo movement, it's a quiet, powerful story about friendship and growing up as a woman.
550: The Villainess's Guide to (Not) Falling in Love by Touya and Ren Sakuma (Square Enix Manga) is a bright, funny villainess romcom. Luciana suddenly remembers her past life and realizes she's the villainess of an otome game, with her public condemnation set to happen in just one year. Her plan is simple: stay far away from every one of the game's love interests. Unfortunately, the harder she avoids them, the more eagerly they pursue her. It's a light, charming read for fans of reverse-harem fantasy.
552: Pupposites Attract by Hono Natsuna (Kodansha) is a cheerful, lighthearted romantic comedy made for dog lovers. Chiharu walks a big Rottweiler, Kiyotaka walks a tiny Pomeranian, and the two keep running into each other at the park. Their pets, and their personalities, don't exactly mesh at first, but all those chance meetings start adding up to something sweeter. It's a fluffy, feel-good read for anyone who has ever made a friend at the dog park.
553: Love Out on a Limb by Yoko Nogiri (Kodansha) is a tangled, heartfelt high school romance from the creator of That Wolf-Boy Is Mine! After eight years apart, Yui moves back to her hometown and into the family home with Hayato, the older brother she hasn't seen since childhood, and her feelings quickly get complicated. Their childhood friend Ritsu offers an unusual fix: a pretend relationship. It's an emotional, drama-filled love triangle for fans of classic shojo romance.
554: Lonely Deaths Lie Thick as Snow by Hajime Inoryu and Shota Ito (Vertical) is a dark, gripping crime thriller for mature readers. In 2006, detective Jin Saeki is sent to check out what looks like a routine burglary at an empty mansion, and instead stumbles onto evidence of horrific crimes that set off a massive manhunt for the owner. When a young woman claiming to be the suspect's daughter comes forward with her own theory, Saeki reluctantly agrees to work with her. It's tense, unsettling, and hard to put down.
555: Cat + Crazy by Wataru Nadatani (Dark Horse) is a goofy, good-hearted comedy from the creator of Cat + Gamer. High schooler Kensuke loves cats more than anything, but his allergic family means he hardly ever gets to be around them. Then he meets an eccentric self-proclaimed cat whisperer and eagerly becomes a disciple, training in the mysterious Cat Fist Way. It's silly, sweet, and full of feline charm, a natural pick for cat lovers and fans of Nadatani's earlier work.
556: Kirio Fan Club by Chikyu no Osakana Ponchan (Vertical) is an absurd, laugh-out-loud high school comedy about friendship and fandom. Aimi and Nami are best friends and rivals, both hopelessly devoted to their classmate Kirio, a boy who barely seems to know they exist. Their attempts to win him over get stranger by the day, from detailed lists of his best qualities to nightly rituals meant to summon him into their dreams. It's silly, messy, and surprisingly sweet about the girls' bond with each other.
557: Betrothed to My Sister's Ex by Tobirano and Chikage Nakakura (Seven Seas) is a tender, healing fantasy romance. Marie has grown up treated like a servant by parents who dote on her older sister, Anastasia. When Anastasia vanishes on her way to marry Duke Kyros and is presumed dead, Marie is sent off in her place, certain she'll only ever be a stand-in. Instead, the duke seems determined to show her otherwise. It's a gentle, comforting read for fans of My Happy Marriage and slow-blooming romance.
559: The Small-Animallike Lady Is Adored by the Ice Prince by Hisui and Mugi Sawai (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny fantasy romance. Liliana, an earl's daughter with no interest in royal life, attends a party held to find a bride for the famously cold Prince William, and to her dismay, he chooses her. She resolves to get out of the engagement as quickly as she can, but the Ice Prince keeps melting a little more every time they meet. It's a fluffy, adorable read for fans of doting-love-interest romcoms.
562: I Want a Gal Gamer to Praise Me by Geshumaro (Yen Press) is a playful gamer romantic comedy. Raito is a shut-in high schooler with big dreams of becoming a top first-person-shooter player, so he enlists Rion, a gyaru who happens to be a seriously skilled gamer, as his coach. Her tips are great; the way she leans in close while he's playing is a lot harder to handle. It's a flirty, lighthearted read for gamers and fans of teasing-romance comedies.
563: Deep 3 by Mitsuhiro Mizuno (Tokyopop) is a driven, high-energy basketball drama. Demian Kawai is a third-year high school player who dreams of becoming a top scorer in the pros, but after a serious injury he develops the yips, a stiffness that locks up his arms whenever he gets close to the basket. His one remaining weapon is the long-range deep three. It's a fast, clean-looking sports story about grit and comebacks, a great pick for fans of Slam Dunk and Kuroko's Basketball.
564: I'm Running for Crown Princess, but All I Want Is a Steady Paycheck! by Yuuri Seo and Makana Watari (Seven Seas) is a bright fantasy romcom with a practical heroine. Therese, the daughter of a broke marquis, works day and night to keep her family afloat. When a knight invites her to compete to become the prince's bride, she laughs it off, until she learns the candidates get paid. Now she's in it for the salary. It's an upbeat read for fans of sensible, hardworking heroines.
565: The Magnificent Bastard by Keiichiro Ryu, Tetsuo Hara, and Mio Aso (Vertical) is a bold, swaggering historical action classic from the artist of Fist of the North Star. In Japan's war-torn Sengoku era, Maeda Keiji is a towering, free-spirited warrior who loves fighting, drinking, and flouting authority, even when the authority is a warlord. He lives by his own code and dares anyone to challenge it. It's larger-than-life samurai adventure with Hara's trademark muscular art, perfect for fans of Vagabond and classic seinen.
566: Hope You're Happy, Lemon by Mizuki Kishikawa (Seven Seas) is a twisty, bittersweet body-swap romance. College student Sunao swore off love after his first girlfriend, Lemon, broke his heart back in junior high. Just as he's ready to try again with a crush from his film club, he runs into Lemon, and after a night under a shooting star he wakes up in her body. Now he has to live her life while searching for a way back. It's an emotional, surprising read for fans of messy, character-driven romance.
568: Chun Rhang Yhur Jhun by Sung-woo Park (Infinity Studios) is a dynamic martial arts epic from the creator of Now. In the mid-7th century, amid the clashes between Tang China and the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo, young warrior Yhun Oh-Rhang is sent to track down his eldest brother in arms, a feared fighter who vanished years ago after leaving to train in China. It's a fast, stylish wuxia-flavored adventure packed with sword fights, perfect for fans of classic martial arts manhwa.
569: Sketchy by Makihirochi (Kodansha) is an uplifting slice-of-life story about trying something new as a grown-up. Ako is in her thirties, working full-time at a movie rental shop and feeling a little stuck, when a skateboarder flies past her in the park and sparks a sudden fascination. Nudged along by a coworker, she signs up for skateboarding lessons alongside two other women with reasons of their own. It's warm, funny, and encouraging, a lovely pick for anyone who's ever wanted to start a hobby late.
570: Assassin & Cinderella by Yuzo Natsuno (Square Enix) is a sultry spy romance for older readers. Neneko is a spy sent to seduce Omi, the ace assassin of a rival organization, and steal his secrets, but he sees through her cover almost immediately. Instead of getting rid of her, he makes an offer: she can keep spying, and he'll protect her from both of their bosses, as long as she marries him. It's a playful, high-stakes romance for readers who like their love stories with a dangerous edge.
572: Team Phoenix by Kenny Ruiz (Udon) is a big-hearted sci-fi adventure that brings together a whole cast of Osamu Tezuka's classic characters. Created by the Spanish artist in collaboration with Tezuka Productions, it's set in a future where an alliance of robots rules most of the universe. Sapphire, a knight troubled by the suffering of those who aren't robots, decides it's time to fight for a different future. It's a colorful, affectionate tribute, a treat for fans of Astro Boy, Princess Knight, and Tezuka's wider universe.
573: 11th Cat by Kim MiKyung (Ice Kunion) is a lively, lighthearted fantasy adventure manhwa. Rika is a clumsy, forgetful girl in training to become a wizard, and a simple quest to find a magic staff goes sideways when she gets lost in the forest and runs into the dark sorcerer who kidnapped the princess. With a loud, cocky cat spirit and a band of friends at her side, she sets out to rescue the princess and prove herself. It's a fun, upbeat read for fans of magical quest stories.
575: Star Project Chiro by Hyekyung Baek (Udon) is a zany, fast-paced romantic comedy manhwa set around the K-pop world. Eun-Yo is pampered and a little vain, thanks to older brothers who treat her like a doll to show off, and she secretly has a crush on a nerdy classmate. When a friend drags her along to sneak into an idol audition, Eun-Yo gets tangled up with a scheming pop singer. It's silly, bouncy fun with lots of exaggerated comic art, great for fans of lighthearted idol romcoms.
576: Flower of the Deep Sleep by Kazumi Yuana (Tokyopop) is a dreamy supernatural shojo drama. Yuuki can glimpse the future in her dreams, and she and her sister Yuuka are promised in marriage to a pair of psychic brothers, an arrangement that gets complicated fast. Then a mysterious girl begins pulling people into a coma-like sleep, and Yuuki must enter their dreams to bring them back. It's a short, atmospheric read for fans of psychic powers, dream worlds, and tangled romance.
577: Metamo Kiss by Sora Omote (Tokyopop) is a playful body-swap romantic comedy. After his grandmother passes away, fourteen-year-old Kohanamaru moves to Tokyo to live with his family, and on his very first day he collides with a girl named Nanao, their lips meet, and they swap bodies. It turns out the men in his family can trade places with their destined partner, and the swap becomes permanent if it isn't undone by sunset. The catch: Nanao likes his twin brother. It's breezy, funny shojo fun.
578: Millennium Prime Minister by Eiki Eiki (Doki Doki) is a soapy, tongue-in-cheek romantic comedy with a political twist. Sixteen-year-old Minori is a tomboyish gamer who handily beats a stranger at the arcade, only to learn he's Kanata, Japan's youngest-ever prime minister, and that he's decided to marry her. Soon she's living at his estate, juggling high school, paparazzi, and a very hostile aide. It's a silly, dramatic read for fans of over-the-top shojo-style romance.
579: Miss Miyazen Would Love to Get Closer to You by Akitaka (Kodansha) is a sweet, gently funny high school romcom. Sakura Miyazen is poised, proper, and quietly curious about her classmate Sota Matsubayashi, a blunt former troublemaker who, as it happens, secretly wants to talk to her too. The trouble is that they come from such different worlds that even saying hello leaves both of them flustered. It's a short, wholesome read for fans of shy, slow-and-steady romance.
580: Momo Tama by Nanae Chrono (Tokyopop) is a zippy supernatural action comedy with roots in the Momotaro folktale, from the creator of Peacemaker Kurogane. Nine-year-old Kokonose is the cocky young head of a clan descended from demons, and a gifted exorcist who has been fighting evil spirits since he was a toddler. With his gloomy twenty-year-old servant Mamoru in tow, he storms the legendary Tougen Island ready to take on all comers. It's energetic, stylish fun for fans of folklore-flavored shonen.
582: Gacha Girls Corps by Chinkururi and Syuu Haruno (Kaiten Books) is a lighthearted isekai adventure built around the thrill of the gacha roll. Heihachi is a devoted mobile gamer who has spent a small fortune on his favorite game when a strange in-game item promises an invitation to another world. One roll later, he's there, under attack by a monster, and saved only by summoning a helmeted knight straight from his phone. It's breezy, game-flavored fun for fans of summoning-system fantasy.
583: Aion by Yuna Kagesaki (Tokyopop) is a moody supernatural action series from the creator of Chibi Vampire. Seine is an immortal girl who hunts mushi, parasitic creatures that take control of people and turn them against one another, using a serpentlike beast called AiON to lure and devour them. When kindhearted orphan Tatsuya gets caught up in her world, he insists on helping, even though her ruthless methods clash with everything he believes. It's a dark, fast-paced read for fans of monster-hunting shonen.
584: Gakuen Prince by Jun Yuzuki (Kodansha) is a rowdy, role-reversal school romantic comedy. Joshi High was an elite all-girls academy until it went coed, and now the girls far outnumber the boys, which means the few young men on campus are fair game. Romance there is less a gentle courtship than an all-out hunt, and the girls are fiercely determined to win. It's a loud, silly, tongue-in-cheek read for fans of reverse-harem chaos and outrageous school comedies.
585: Takeru: Opera Susanoh Sword of the Devil by Kazuki Nakashima and Karakarakemuri (Tokyopop) is a rollicking mythic fantasy adventure from the writer of Gurren Lagann. On the islands of Oyashima, a militant kingdom is waging a brutal war of conquest. Into the middle of it strolls Izumo-no-Takeru, a cheerful soldier of fortune hunting for clues to the legendary Sword of Susanoh, and he soon teams up with two other wanderers who share his name. It's bold, energetic action steeped in Japanese myth.
587: Ghost Reaper Girl by Akissa Saike (Viz Media) is a zany supernatural action comedy from the creator of Rosario+Vampire. Chloé is a struggling actress best known for a cheesy late-night show about a monster-slaying schoolgirl, even though she's actually pushing thirty. When demons escaped from hell start turning up in real life, she finds herself mysteriously attractive to them, and a demon hunter who happens to be her biggest fan proposes a pact to fight them together. It's silly, energetic fun for fans of oddball supernatural shonen.
588: Monochrome Factor by Kaili Sorano (Tokyopop) is a stylish supernatural action series. Akira is a laid-back high schooler who would rather skip class than care about anything, until a mysterious man named Shirogane appears and insists that Akira is meant to fight beside him. Soon Akira is drawn into the hidden world of shadows, where strange creatures threaten the balance between light and dark. It's a moody, good-looking read for fans of bishonen and urban fantasy.
589: Mononoke Sharing by coolkyousinnjya (Seven Seas) is a goofy, cozy supernatural comedy from the creator of Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid. High schooler Yata shares a cheap old house with five yokai roommates, including a laid-back kappa, a horned devil, a flirty fox spirit, a stay-at-home rokurokubi, and a shy snow woman. Their everyday mishaps play out in short slice-of-life chapters with a gentle message about outsiders finding a place to belong. It's light, cheeky fun for fans of monster-girl comedies, with plenty of grown-up jokes.
590: MonsTABOO by Yuya Takahashi (Yen Press) is a dark, strange monster romance for mature readers. Maruka looks like a model honor student, but she secretly believes the world is full of monsters disguised as grown-ups, and she has been hoping to meet one that will end her life. Instead, a rabbit-like monster saves her, and she starts to wonder whether he might be something closer to a soulmate. It's an offbeat, unsettling blend of horror, action, and romance for readers who like their love stories weird.
591: Monster Collection by Sei Itoh (CMX) is a classic swords-and-sorcery adventure based on a Japanese collectible card game. Kasche is a spirited young summoner studying at a magic academy when dark forces steal a powerful spellbook from a neighboring kingdom, and she's sent to get it back. Along the way she gathers a colorful band of companions, including a cynical dagger-wielding warrior, a shapeshifting lamia, and a sharp-tongued lizard king. It's a fun, old-school fantasy quest for fans of monster-summoning adventures.
592: Monster Hunter Orage by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a lively fantasy action series based on the hit video game, from the creator of Fairy Tail. Shiki is a young, hotheaded hunter with big ambitions, and he sets out to gather a team strong enough to track down a legendary monster. Along the way, he and his new companions take on huge beasts, forge new weapons, and learn to fight as a team. It's fast, fun, and full of action, a great pick for gamers and Mashima fans alike.
593: Muscles Are Better Than Magic! by Doraneko and Kouji Onodera (Seven Seas) is a goofy, good-natured fantasy comedy. Yuri has spent ten years alone in a forest doing nothing but training, and the result is a body that can solve just about any problem with brute force. When a lost elf named Filia stumbles into his home and asks for help getting out of the woods, the two set off on a journey neither of them is quite prepared for. It's lighthearted, punchy fun for fans of fantasy parody.
594: Alice on Deadlines by Shiro Ihara (Yen Press) is a wacky supernatural body-swap comedy with a grim-reaper twist. Lapan is a lecherous young death god who's disappointed to be sent to the human world as a mere skeleton, until a mishap lands him in the body of sweet, kindhearted Alice, while she ends up stuck in his bony form. Now the mismatched pair have to muddle through together while Lapan figures out what he's lost. It's silly, fast-paced fun for fans of offbeat shinigami stories.
595: Alice the 101st by Chigusa Kawai (Doki Doki) is a lively school drama set in the world of classical music. The prestigious Mondonville Music Academy admits only 100 students a year, but fourteen-year-old country boy Aristide "Alice" Lang impresses the board so much that he's let in as the 101st. He can't read sheet music and knows almost no theory, but he has a remarkable ear and memory. It's an energetic, warmhearted read for fans of music-school stories and quirky ensemble casts.
596: Tenjho Tenge by Oh! Great (Viz Media) is a hard-hitting martial arts action series with a mature edge. Souichiro Nagi and his friend Bob arrive at Todo Academy planning to fight their way to the top, only to discover the school is ruled by clubs of serious martial artists. A run-in with the Juken Club pulls them into a much bigger and older conflict. It's a stylish, violent brawler for readers who like intense fight scenes and detailed art.
598: Glitch by Shima Shinya (Yen Press) is a dreamy, quietly eerie sci-fi mystery. When siblings Minato and Akira move to a new town, they find it full of strange sights: shadowy figures at bus stops, foxes as tall as mountains, shopkeepers with wings for heads. The locals call them glitches and barely notice them, but Akira and her new school friends can't help wanting to know more. It's a gentle, atmospheric read full of lovely imagery, perfect for fans of Mushishi and slow, wondering mysteries.
599: God Bless the Mistaken by Nio Nakatani (Yen Press) is a quiet, melancholy slice-of-life drama with a supernatural twist, from the creator of Bloom Into You. In a shrinking rural town of empty buildings and near-empty classrooms, strange phenomena called bugs keep appearing. Teenage Kon lives with his landlady Kasane, the town's leading bugs researcher, and helps with her work as her unofficial assistant. It's an understated, atmospheric story for readers who enjoy slow, thoughtful manga about small places and the people who stay.
